page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Last call for Tom
title: Last call for Tom
topic: Language to say you've changed your mind
description:
Our story has got rather dramatic. Anna has realised that Tom is really the man for her so she's on her way to the airport to try and catch him before he boards his flight to Australia and his new life on the other side of the world. But will Anna be able to convince Tom that she's changed her mind?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use to explain that you've changed your mind.
phrases: I've been doing a lot of thinking.
I didn't realise how much I missed you until you had gone.
I've changed my mind, I will marry you!

listening_challenge.question: What class does Tom claim he always flies in?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello and welcome to English at Work where things have got rather dramatic.  Anna is on her way to the airport to try and catch Tom before he boards his flight to Australia and his new life on the other side of the world. But will she get there in time?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. Excuse me, do you know where the check in desks for flights to Sydney are?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Yeah, over there luv – desk number 47.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: … yeah, I always fly business class, it's the kind of guy I am… shame you're not available to fly with me but you know…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, Tom!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna? How… what… what are you doing here?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Don't go… we need you… I need you.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: But I don’t understand… you rejected me.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes but… but…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: But what Anna? What are you going to say? How can you tell him you were wrong and you've changed your mind?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hmm, I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Passenger 1
transcript.text: Tell him 'I've been doing a lot of thinking'.

transcript.speaker: Passenger 2
transcript.text: Say, 'I didn't realise how much I missed you until you had gone'.

transcript.speaker: Passenger 3
transcript.text: And tell him, 'I've changed my mind, I will marry you!'

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, I heard all that and that other man who you're always talking to.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh right!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. Well Tom, will you marry me?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Why should I after all you've put me through?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yeah why should he?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Because Tom… you're a funny guy and… I love you and… I can't live without you.

transcript.speaker: Passengers
transcript.text: Ahhh!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Let me think about this … oh if you put it like that then yes, I will marry you!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh Tom!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hooray. At last! We got there in the end but not without using these phrases:
I've been doing a lot of thinking.
I didn't realise how much I missed you until you had gone.
I've changed my mind, I will marry you!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And…
I love you and I can't live without you!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I won't be needing these anymore.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Join us very soon for the English at Work wedding of the year. Bye!
